transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Zhang (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Lee (Redwood Solutions); Carlos Ruiz (Head of ML, Nimbus Search); Priya Nair (Infra); Tom Reynolds (Product); Jordan (Data Scientist)

[00:00:00] Alice: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we're gonna jump into embeddings and reranking perf and cost, um Samir's gonna lead most of the bench details, I'll help with commercial and topology questions
[00:00:12] Carlos: great thanks, quick context - we have a candidate generation + rerank pipeline, typical user queries return ~200-1,000 candidates; target p95 latency for rerank path 120ms end-to-end, and SLO for interactive UI is 200ms. cost is also a big driver, so we want to understand dims/batching/quantization tradeoffs
[00:00:30] Samir: got it; first thing to align on - are you doing dense vector similarity for rerank only, or running model-based cross-encoder rerank? sounds like you do a two-stage: sparse/dense retrieval then a cross-encoder rerank on top?
[00:00:42] Jordan: yeah two-stage, candidates from retrieval then cross-encoder on the top N - usually N is 100 but sometimes 500 or 1k for offline, UI uses 100
[00:00:52] Samir: ok perfect. so two distinct workloads: embeddings generation (if you do it online) and the cross-encoder scoring. today we'll focus on cross-encoder-style rerank perf and the cost profile if you choose to move parts to Dedicated or Private
[00:01:10] Priya: one quick infra note - our infra team prefers VPC deployment and strict egress rules; we likely need private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering, and audit logs must be retained 90 days
[00:01:22] Maya: noted, Redwood Private supports on-prem/VPC, and we can enable KMS for keys and streaming audit logs to your SIEM

-- Technical baseline and metrics --
[00:02:00] Samir: baseline assumptions for today's numbers: model footprints as a proxy - small cross-encoder (≈110M) vs medium (≈340M) vs large (≈1.2B). embedding dims we'll test at 128, 512, 768. latency SLO targets we'll compare: p50/p95 for single-request rerank for N=100, batch sizes we'll consider both request batching (multiple queries per forward) and candidate batching (score multiple candidates in a single forward)
[00:02:30] Tom: can you clarify candidate batching?
[00:02:34] Samir: yeah candidate batching = instead of running N separate forward passes for query-candidate pairs, we build a matrix of shape (N, dim) and run a single forward that scores all candidates against the query via optimized matrix ops or fused kernels - this benefits from larger batch sizes but can increase tail latency if you accumulate candidates
[00:02:54] Carlos: so for N=100, if we batch all 100 it's one big op - latency depends on GPU memory and kernel perf, right?
[00:03:00] Samir: exactly. on an A10/A100 class GPU, scoring 100 pairs with medium model can be ~30-60ms with fp16, single-shot. with int8 or 4-bit quant, it drops further but we need to validate quality impact

[00:03:30] Samir: couple of tradeoffs:
- vector dim: higher dims -> more memory and compute but better retrieval quality; dims 128 vs 512 vs 768 shows linear-ish compute cost but quality gains plateau depending on dataset
- batch size: larger batches improve throughput but increase p95; for UI you'll choose smaller batches or async partial responses
- KV cache: for generation we use KV cache; for rerank it's less relevant unless you're caching embeddings for candidate vectors to avoid re-embedding; Redwood's cache supports prefix caching of embeddings and per-customer TTLs

[00:04:10] Priya: about KV cache for embeddings - we'd want candidate vectors cached and shared across requests; is cache hot-shard tolerant and does it persist across restarts?
[00:04:20] Samir: yes cache is persistent on Dedicated/Private, with configurable TTL and replication. For hosted there's an LRU in-memory plus optional redis-backed persistent cache. For Private you can point to your Redis or use our embedded cache with encrypted persistence

[00:04:45] Carlos: curious numbers - can you run through typical QPS/latency for different dims and batch sizes?
[00:04:50] Samir: sure here's an approximate table I read out (these are synthetic numbers we usually use as a starting point):
- 128-dim candidate scoring (small model, fp16): single query N=100, no batching: p50 18ms p95 40ms; throughput ~450 qps on A100 streaming scenario
- 512-dim (medium model): single-shot N=100: p50 32ms p95 70ms; throughput ~220 qps
- 768-dim (larger): p50 50ms p95 120ms; throughput ~140 qps
Quantized (int8/4-bit) often reduces latency 20-35% depending on kernel support

[00:05:40] Tom: those p95s for 768 look close to our 120ms SLO, but that's just rerank CPU/GPU time - we need end-to-end (network + retrieval + UI). so buffer needed
[00:05:52] Samir: correct. typical buffer we recommend is keep rerank p95 under 60-80ms for UI SLO 200ms. to do that you either: reduce dims, reduce N, or enable async progressive results where top-k are scored first

[00:06:15] Jordan: progressive scoring - can Redwood stream partial rerank results while finishing the rest?
[00:06:20] Maya: yes, we support streaming and can surface the top-k as soon as they are ready; can also route to a fallback cheaper model if the main path is congested

-- Quantization & model artifacts --
[00:06:40] Samir: about quantization - we support fp16, int8, and experimental 4-bit kernels. int8 typically has minimal quality loss for cross-encoder scoring but depends on calibration; 4-bit can be great for throughput but you must validate NDCG/accuracy on your rerank labels
[00:06:58] Carlos: have you seen cases where int8 destroyed rerank ordering?
[00:07:02] Samir: rare for scoring models; more common for generation LM outputs. For cross-encoders, calibration and per-layer clipping solves most issues. we run eval harnesses for that and can share the evaluation reports

[00:07:25] Priya: memory footprint - for 512-dim medium model what's GPU RAM usage when batching N=100?
[00:07:30] Samir: roughly for medium model fp16 + activations + workspace you're looking at 8-10GB for scoring 100 candidates in one pass on A100; quantized int8 can bring that down to ~5-6GB. of course these are approximate and vary by model and kernel selection

[00:07:52] Tom: what about CPU-only? we have some cheaper nodes and want to failover to CPU for low QPS - how does throughput look?
[00:07:58] Samir: CPU inference for cross-encoder scoring is much slower. On 32-core Xeon you might get 10-30 qps for medium model N=100, p95s in hundreds of ms. For cost/latency sensitive interactive UI we recommend GPU. CPU fallback is fine for background/batch reranks

-- Deployment and networking --
[00:08:30] Priya: VPC - we need private endpoints and no egress. can Dedicated support VPC peering with our VPC and private subnets?
[00:08:38] Maya: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private deployment gives you full control. For strict no-egress we recommend Private (customer-managed control plane) or Dedicated with egress rounded down depending on contract. Audit logs to your SIEM are supported

[00:08:55] Carlos: if we go Private on-prem, do you support GPU pass-through and our internal HSM?
[00:09:00] Maya: we support on-prem bundles, GPU passthrough, and integrations with customer KMS/HSM for key management. would need an infra runbook exchange though

-- Cost discussion --
[00:09:20] Alice: pricing quick notes - embeddings and rerank are charged differently: embedding generation per-embed unit, cross-encoder scoring we price per inference-second and reserved Dedicated capacity can lower unit cost significantly. We'll share the pricing sheet but expect 30-50% unit cost reduction for Dedicated for sustained throughput
[00:09:40] Carlos: can you quantify example cost per 1k queries for N=100?
[00:09:44] Alice: rough ballpark - hosted fp16 medium model rerank might be $0.15 - $0.30 per 1k queries depending on batching and QPS; Dedicated pricing for similar sustained load could be ~$0.08 - $0.12 per 1k given reserved commits. exacts depend on batch efficiency and cache hit rates

[00:10:10] Jordan: cache hit rates - if we cache embeddings for candidates we reduce computation - what's realistic hit rate?
[00:10:16] Samir: depends on candidate churn; for ecomm-like catalogs with slow change you could see 70-90% cache hit on candidate vectors; for news or fast-feed apps lower. cache hits translate linearly to cost savings for the scoring stage if you avoid re-embedding heavy steps

-- Benchmarks and pilot plan --
[00:10:40] Samir: proposed pilot: we run a 1k-query rerank benchmark across dims 128/512/768, N=100 and N=500, on both fp16 and int8, on a Dedicated GPU (A10-like) and on Private if you want. We'll produce p50/p95, throughput, memory, and cost estimates. We need sample candidate payloads, labels (if any), and expected SLOs
[00:11:04] Carlos: we'll provide sample payloads and a small labeled set for quality checks; can you include quantization eval (NDCG) in the report?
[00:11:10] Samir: yes we'll include NDCG/accuracy delta vs fp16 baseline. We also link to a benchmark spreadsheet - we'll share after the call

[00:11:24] Tom: one last question: if we need to guarantee 120ms p95 UI, and we expect spikes, any recommended architecture?
[00:11:31] Samir: a few patterns:
- use a cheap fallback model for overflow (std model routing)
- progressive/ranked streaming so top-10 appear fast
- provision some headroom in Dedicated capacity and autoscale burst pools
- pre-warm cache for predictable queries

[00:11:55] Carlos: ok makes sense. can we get a spec of the Dedicated topology you recommend for our expected baseline QPS of 60 - 120?
[00:12:02] Alice: we'll include recommended Dedicated pool sizing in the pricing/benchmark doc. also include expected memory and GPU type mappings

-- Closing & recap --
[00:12:30] Alice: recap: Redwood to share benchmark config + pricing; Samir to run bench and include quantization eval; Nimbus to send payloads and SLOs by Friday; follow up meeting to review results next week. Any other open items?
[00:12:48] Priya: one small note - we need SOC2 report and customer security addendum; please attach to the follow-up email
[00:12:55] Maya: will include SOC2, network diagrams, and Private runbook extract
[00:13:05] Carlos: thanks everyone, this was helpful
[00:13:09] Alice: thanks all, we'll follow up.
